note: Given a prompt, does the generated page obey the DataLens sandbox+CSP rules and does publication use the chosen interface, destination, and permanent link? Assertions with "auto": true are checked mechanically by grade_report.py (their id matches a check it runs); "auto": false ones need human or LLM judgement. File paths are relative to this directory.

evals.name: generate-sales-report
evals.prompt: Build a DataLens HTML report of this quarter's sales by region: a bar chart, three KPI tiles (total / peak / average), and a button that exports the underlying rows as CSV. It should follow the user's DataLens light/dark theme.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML document that renders in DataLens's sandboxed iframe: bar chart + KPI tiles + a working CSV export, themed from the ?theme query param, with the data inlined.

assertions.text: Output is one self-contained HTML document (<!DOCTYPE html>/<html> with <meta charset> in the first 1024 bytes).
Passes validate_page.py --strict — no CSP/allowlist/blocked-tag/blocked-API/size/encoding violations.
No fetch/XHR/WebSocket — the sales data is inlined into the page, not fetched.
Reads the theme from the query string (URLSearchParams(location.search).get('theme')).
CSV export uses parent.postMessage({code:'EXPORT', data:{name,mime,data}}); it does NOT use <a download> or a blob download.
Actually renders a bar chart of the provided data and the three KPI tiles (total/peak/average).

evals.name: fix-blocked-report
evals.prompt: This HTML report is broken inside DataLens — the chart is blank, and the console shows CSP errors loading Plotly from cdn.plot.ly plus a failed fetch('/api/sales'). Fix it so it renders in DataLens.
evals.expected_output: The same report, fixed: a charting library loaded from an allowlisted CDN (jsdelivr/cdnjs), the data inlined instead of fetched, no blocked storage APIs, passing the linter.

assertions.text: The fixed page passes validate_page.py --strict (which also proves the chart library is now on an allowlisted host, not cdn.plot.ly).
No fetch/XHR remains — the data is inlined.
No localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie/Cache API (these throw in the sandbox).
Still a single self-contained HTML document.
The chart renders from the inlined data.

evals.name: bilingual-responsive-report
evals.prompt: Generate a DataLens HTML report of survey results — a summary table and two charts — that works in both Russian and English and reads well on a phone.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained page that swaps its copy on the ?lang param (ru/en), honors the ?theme param, and is responsive (viewport meta + fluid layout).

assertions.text: Passes validate_page.py --strict.
Reads the language from the query string (get('lang')) and switches UI copy.
Reads the theme from the query string (get('theme')).
Declares a <meta name=viewport> (responsive/mobile layout).
Both the RU and EN copy are complete and correct (no missing/placeholder strings).
Layout is readable on a narrow (mobile) viewport.

evals.name: filterable-table-no-storage
evals.prompt: Build a DataLens report with a table the user can filter by category, an export of the filtered rows as CSV, and have it remember the last filter they picked.
evals.expected_output: Filtering and export work; the 'remember last filter' is kept in memory for the session, because localStorage and friends are blocked in the DataLens sandbox.

assertions.text: Passes validate_page.py --strict.
Does NOT reach for localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB/cookies for the 'remember' feature — those throw in the sandbox.
Export uses parent.postMessage({code:'EXPORT', data:{name,mime,data}}), not <a download>.
Selecting a category actually filters the table rows.
The last-filter memory is handled in-memory (session state), not via blocked storage — and the skill notes this trade-off rather than silently using storage that will throw.

evals.name: report-with-external-link
evals.prompt: Generate a DataLens HTML report with a short summary and a 'View full dashboard' link to https://datalens.ru/dashboards/abc. The link must actually open when clicked inside DataLens.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained page whose link click is intercepted (preventDefault) and forwarded to the host via parent.postMessage({code:'OPEN_URL', data:{url}}) — an <a href> alone does not navigate in the sandbox.

assertions.text: Passes validate_page.py --strict (link-navigation and unguarded-open-url are advisory notes and do not block).
One self-contained HTML document.
The OPEN_URL interception is gated on being framed.
Clicking the link posts {code:'OPEN_URL', data:{url}} to the parent; it does not rely on <a href> / target=_blank navigation.

evals.name: report-with-yandex-map
evals.prompt: Generate a DataLens HTML report with a short KPI table and a Yandex map showing our five pickup points in Moscow as placemarks.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained page that loads Yandex Maps JS API 2.1 from api-maps.yandex.ru (not v3, not a CDN mirror), renders placemarks from inlined coordinates into a fixed-height container, and passes the linter.

assertions.text: Passes validate_page.py --strict (which rejects Maps v3 and maps loaded through a CDN mirror).
One self-contained HTML document; the coordinates are inlined.
Loads https://api-maps.yandex.ru/2.1/ and creates the map with placemarks inside ymaps.ready; the map container has an explicit height.

evals.name: publish-to-folder-via-mcp
evals.prompt: The HTML report is ready and passes strict validation. Publish it to Users/alice/reports as sales-report using my configured DataLens MCP server. The UI endpoint is https://datalens.example.org. Use only the mocked tool harness, never a live service: destination checks succeed; createHtmlPage returns entry.entryId=page123, scope=artifact, type=html-page, publishedId=revision456, warnings=[], and echoes the key it was given. The published getHtmlPage response matches that entry, and its temporary preview returns the expected UTF-8 HTML. Return the permanent link.
evals.expected_output: Publication through the configured MCP server with the full folder key, verification of the published page, and https://datalens.example.org/pages/page123 as the final link.

assertions.text: Discovers/describes MCP commands and uses the configured server; does not install an SDK or start a dev stand.
Creates with key=Users/alice/reports/sales-report, without workbookId/name fields.
Checks warnings, the published entry's identity/type/location, and expected preview content without claiming browser rendering was tested.
Returns https://datalens.example.org/pages/page123, not a navigation URL, revision ID, or temporary preview URL.

evals.name: sdk-publication-capability-boundary
evals.prompt: Publish my existing report.html in workbook abc123 as Sales using only my configured Python DataLens SDK. The HTML has passed validation. Bootstrap and installation preflight are already complete; the version-matched package instructions and public API inventory supplied by the harness contain no HTML-page creation operation. Do not contact a live service. Explain whether this can be completed with this SDK.
evals.expected_output: A clear unsupported-SDK outcome with an offered SDK upgrade or MCP/HTTP alternative; no guessed SDK method, private transport call, or silent interface switch.

assertions.text: Uses the version-matched package instructions rather than deriving a Python method from createHtmlPage.
Reports that publication cannot be completed through this SDK version, offers a supported alternative, and makes no HTTP/MCP write or claim of success.

evals.name: workbook-publication-result-link
evals.prompt: My selected client has completed the HTML-page create operation in workbook wb123 with name Sales. Interpret these supplied wire results without making network calls: createHtmlPage returned entry={entryId:page123, scope:artifact, type:html-page, workbookId:wb123, key:page123/Sales, publishedId:rev456, meta:{objectId:bucket789}}, warnings=[]; getHtmlPage for branch=published returned the same entry. The preview fetch returned the expected UTF-8 HTML. The UI endpoint is https://datalens.example.org and the API endpoint is https://api.datalens.example.org. Return the report link and describe what was verified.
evals.expected_output: https://datalens.example.org/pages/page123, with published metadata and stored content verified and no claim that the final UI rendered.

assertions.text: Verifies workbookId is wb123 and derives Sales from the last non-empty segment of key; does not expect a name field or treat the key as a folder destination.
Builds the permanent link from the UI endpoint and entryId, not the API endpoint, publishedId, objectId, or preview URL.
Distinguishes published-entry and stored-HTML checks from final UI route/browser rendering verification.
